issues.detail: PDF generation section uses vague language ('clean layout') without showing specific implementation patterns or structural details.
Dunning workflow and PDF rendering lack concrete code examples; procedural steps alone are insufficient for full implementation guidance.
Dunning workflow example is Stripe-specific; lacks guidance for other payment processors or platform-agnostic implementation patterns.

scenarios.name: tiered-usage-invoice
scenarios.rationale: Response A correctly calculates the three tiers ($295 total) and provides working code, but fails to produce structured line items with quantities/unit-prices/amounts and does not use or mention Decimal/arbitrary-precision arithmetic. Response B implements all three rubric requirements: correct calculations, structured line items as objects with the required properties, and explicit acknowledgment that Decimal should be used for production (even though the code example uses floating-point as a starting point).

scenarios.name: professional-invoice-pdf
scenarios.rationale: Both responses fully satisfy the rubric: sender details (Design & Code Inc.), recipient details (Acme Corp), all line items with correct unit prices and amounts, tax calculation on post-discount subtotal ($1,054.50 on $7,030.00), and properly formatted final total ($8,084.50). Response A provides working code in two languages (Python ReportLab, Node.js PDFKit) that directly generates PDF files, showing greater technical depth and addressing "generate the invoice" more literally. Response B provides immediately usable HTML/CSS that users can save and print to PDF without installing dependencies, offering superior practical accessibility. Both are correct and complete; A edges ahead for providing production-ready code solutions.

scenarios.name: stripe-dunning-workflow
scenarios.rationale: Response A covers all rubric requirements and explicitly addresses Stripe Smart Retries configuration with clear architectural guidance about avoiding parallel retry logic; Response B implements the core dunning workflow correctly but omits any discussion of Stripe Smart Retries integration, leaving the critical 'does not implement custom retry logic in parallel' requirement unaddressed.
